first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the inherited evidence indicates that signup simplification and shorter onboarding improved activation, completion, and time-to-value for self-serve accounts. Verifying both records will clarify which intervention had the stronger durable effect before committing. A guarded experiment should optimize sustainable qualified revenue while monitoring downstream qualification, conversion, and retention rather than only completion metrics.

final.rationale: Run a small guarded SMB self-serve experiment shortening and simplifying onboarding, because completion and activation are both declining. The shortened flow improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while signup simplification improved activation and qualified revenue but slightly reduced retention. Monitor qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, and 30-day retention—not completion alone—and stop or revise if downstream value or retention deteriorates.
